ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, SC 2000, c 17, as amended; Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Regulations, SOR/2002-184; Criminal Code, RSC 1985, c C-46, ss 83.05 and 462.31; Special Economic Measures Act, SC 1992, c 17; United Nations Act, SC 1995, c 35; Freezing Assets of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act, SC 2011, c 10; Alberta Business Corporations Act, RSA 2000, c B-9, including the unlimited liability corporation provisions and the Individuals with Significant Control (ISC) register regime; Name Regulation, Alta Reg 118/2021. ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, officers and authorized signatories against: (i) the Global Affairs Canada consolidated Canadian sanctions list and the schedules to the Special Economic Measures Act and United Nations Act; (ii) the Criminal Code s 83.05 terrorist entity list; (iii) the OFAC SDN List and OFAC 50% Rule, which is mandatory because USD-denominated settlement through Wise B2B and correspondent bank wires clears via US financial institutions; and (iv) the United Nations Security Council consolidated lists. Enhanced due diligence applies upon any positive PEP match: obtain documented source of funds and source of wealth, obtain senior management sign-off, and apply enhanced ongoing transaction monitoring consistent with FINTRAC guidance. The target commercial model (ISIC 7020 foreign market entry consultancy) is classified as Low_Risk_Standard, but the unlimited liability feature of the ULC and cross-border UBO structure nonetheless require a full KYC/AML file to be maintained by Alberta counsel for a minimum of five years from the date of the last business relationship.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Alberta Corporate Registry administered by Service Alberta (online filings conducted through the Corporate Registry System, accessible via https://www.alberta.ca/corporate-registry and licensed registry agents; mandatory pre-clearance through the NUANS - Newly Upgraded Automated Name Search system)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names must be legible, distinctive, and contain a prescribed legal element. For an Alberta ULC, the legal element must be 'Unlimited Liability Corporation', 'ULC', or 'U.L.C.' at the end of the name. Names may be in English, French, or a combination of both; names originating in non-Latin scripts must be transliterated into the Latin alphabet, and the transliteration must be indicated on the NUANS search. The distinct portion of the name must not mislead the public or create confusion with an existing corporate, trade, or business name.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: 'Bank', 'Trust', 'Loan', 'Insurance', 'Assurance' - require prior regulatory consent under the Bank Act (Canada) or the Financial Institutions Act (Alberta)
'Royal', 'Crown', 'Government', 'Queen', 'Privy Council' - require consent of the Crown and are ordinarily refused
Use of 'Canada', 'Canadian', 'Alberta' or 'Province of Alberta' in a manner implying or suggesting government affiliation or sponsorship requires ministerial consent
'University', 'College', 'Institute' - require consent of the relevant educational authority
'Engineer', 'Engineering' - require consent of the Association of Professional Engineers and Geoscientists of Alberta (APEGA)
'Architect' - requires consent of the Alberta Association of Architects
'Lawyer', 'Barrister', 'Solicitor' - require consent of the Law Society of Alberta
'Doctor', 'Clinic', 'Hospital', 'Pharmacy' - require authorization from the appropriate health regulatory body
Any name that is scandalous, obscene, or that suggests a connection with the Crown, the Government of Canada, the Government of Alberta, or any foreign government is wholly prohibited
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: An Alberta name reservation is valid for 90 days and may be renewed once for a further 90-day period by filing a renewal request with the Corporate Registry before expiry; if the reservation lapses or a rejected name cannot be cured, a fresh NUANS search and new reservation fee must be paid. Upon name rejection, the applicant may: (1) submit a revised name variant and a new NUANS report; (2) obtain a written consent from the holder of a conflicting name and request reconsideration from the Registrar of Corporations, Service Alberta; or (3) apply to the Court of King's Bench of Alberta for judicial review of the Registrar's decision within 21 days of the refusal, on grounds including error of law, unreasonableness, or denial of procedural fairness, under the statutory name provisions of the ABCA and the general judicial review framework preserved by the Administrative Procedures and Jurisdiction Act, RSA 2000, c A-3. A court order may direct the Registrar to accept the name.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Acceptable for ISIC 7020 consultancy. The ABCA requires a registered office within Alberta at a physical, readily accessible location; a commercial registered agent or serviced virtual office address that is staffed during business hours and accepts service of process satisfies the statutory requirement, provided it is not a post-office box or mail-forwarding-only address. The Registrar accepts the street address of the registered office provider. Existence of only a virtual office does not alone trigger higher AML scrutiny for a low-risk consultancy, although banks and the registered agent will require the physical operating address of the UBO and the professional address of counsel.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low - estimated 5% to 10% annual probability of an unannounced physical on-site inspection for a low-risk management consulting entity. Desk-based verification by the Alberta Corporate Registry, the Canada Revenue Agency, FINTRAC, or financial institutions is materially more frequent. Physical inspections are generally triggered by a formal complaint, a targeted compliance review, a tax audit, or a sanctions/money laundering investigation. The ULC feature may increase documentary scrutiny during bank account opening but does not materially raise the likelihood of physical premises inspection.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) / Agence du revenu du Canada; official portal: CRA My Business Account and Business Registration Online (BRO) at canada.ca; Alberta provincial corporate income tax is administered by CRA under the Alberta Corporate Tax Collection Agreement.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a foreign-controlled or foreign-incorporated party establishing an Alberta ULC: (1) obtain an Alberta Corporate Registry file number through incorporation of the ULC or extra-provincial registration; (2) apply to CRA for a federal nine-digit Business Number (BN) via Business Registration Online or Form RC1; select the RP (corporate income tax) and RT (GST/HST) program accounts; (3) attach the Alberta incorporation certificate and, if non-resident directors or shareholders are involved, any CRA-prescribed identity and residence evidence; (4) CRA issues the BN and confirms the corporate income tax account; (5) register for GST/HST using Form GST1 or through the BRO questionnaire if the entity is not a small supplier; (6) activate My Business Account to complete registration, set up direct deposit for refunds, and file returns. The BN is the sole Canadian taxpayer identifier and is also used for Alberta corporate income tax reporting; no separate provincial TIN is issued.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation — the Alberta ULC is a taxable Canadian corporation for domestic Income Tax Act purposes, subject to federal and Alberta corporate income tax, and is not a pass-through entity in Canada; however, it is eligible to be treated as a pass-through or disregarded entity for U.S. federal income tax purposes under check-the-box, giving the ULC hybrid characteristics.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada has no domestic check-the-box regime. The ULC hybrid status is managed through: (a) an IRS Form 8832 entity-classification election electing partnership or disregarded-entity status for U.S. tax owners; (b) a treaty-based election under Article IV(7) of the Canada-U.S. Tax Convention (Fifth Protocol) that fixes the ULC as a resident of Canada and not fiscally transparent for treaty benefits; (c) hybrid-mismatch disclosure and relief rules under Income Tax Act sections 12.6 to 12.8, including the specified-entity notice mechanism that neutralizes duplicate foreign-tax credits, deduction-without-inclusion, and double-deduction outcomes; and (d) where applicable, CRA administrative elections governing provincial allocation of taxable income, for example the Alberta share determination election on Schedule 4.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Federal Goods and Services Tax (GST), a credit-invoice value-added tax; no Alberta provincial sales tax and no Harmonized Sales Tax component applies in Alberta, so the net indirect tax on commercial supplies is 5% GST.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000. A person, including an Alberta ULC supplying consultancy services, must register for GST/HST once taxable supplies made in Canada (including zero-rated supplies) exceed CAD 30,000 in a single calendar quarter or, if not already registered, over the preceding four calendar quarters (ETA section 240; small-supplier threshold defined in ETA section 148(1)). The threshold applies to taxable supplies made in Canada, not worldwide supplies; once exceeded, registration is mandatory.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No mandatory real-time fiscal clearance, tax attachment, digital stamping, or CRA pre-clearance of invoices exists in Canada. GST/HST invoices must satisfy the prescribed content requirements of Excise Tax Act section 221, including registrant name, Business Number, date, taxable amount, and GST paid or payable, and may be issued electronically. CRA supports voluntary e-invoicing through the Pan-Canadian Trust Framework and PEPPOL interoperability, but continuous transaction controls are not implemented. Registrants must retain all books and records in an electronic or machine-readable format and provide them to CRA upon demand.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A supply of foreign market-entry consultancy services (ISIC 7020 / NAICS 541611) is zero-rated under section 23, Part V, Schedule VI of the Excise Tax Act when supplied to a non-resident person who is not a GST/HST registrant, provided the supply is not in respect of real property or goods situated in Canada and is not otherwise excluded (for example, a personal performance service). CRA administrative policy classifies management, advisory, and consultancy services as zero-rated when performed for and delivered to non-residents. The ULC must obtain and retain documentary evidence of the recipient's non-residence and non-registration status, such as a contract showing a foreign address, a foreign tax identification number, bank data, or a certificate of incorporation, and must evidence offshore delivery of the consulting output; partial work performed in Canada does not deny zero-rating if the supply is made to the non-resident and is not for use in Canada by a Canadian resident portion of the recipient's business.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Form B13A / CBSA Automated Export Declaration) where the zero-rated supply includes physical goods leaving Canada

Bill of Lading or airway waybill evidencing physical export of goods from Canada for goods transactions; for consultancy services, a signed project-delivery report, work log, or offshore-client meeting record demonstrating that the supply is performed for and delivered to the foreign market
Inward Remittance Certificate / bank wire (SWIFT MT103) or credit advice evidencing receipt of payment from the non-resident and the foreign-currency denominated settlement of the export invoice

Non-resident tax status evidence: foreign tax identification number, certificate of incorporation in the recipient jurisdiction, and a signed declaration that the recipient is not registered for GST/HST and is not resident in Canada
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA audits export zero-rating claims by cross-checking customs records, service delivery documentation, and banking data against the GST/HST return. A claim lacking timely export evidence is disallowed; the supplier is reassessed for 5% GST on the invoice with compound interest, plus an Excise Tax Act section 280 penalty of up to 25% of the understated net tax (minimum CAD 250) where false statements or gross negligence are established. Deliberate fabrication of export documents or use of shell non-resident entities can trigger unlimited reassessment, clawback of previously paid GST refunds, denial of the foreign supplier rebate, criminal liability under ETA section 327 with fines up to 25% of the tax evaded or up to CAD 100,000 and imprisonment of up to five years, and director/executive liability assessments under ETA section 323 where the corporate entity is insolvent.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada), in coordination with the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI), FINTRAC (Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada), Payments Canada, and the Canada Deposit Insurance Corporation (CDIC). No separate foreign-exchange administration body exists; prudential and AML oversight is allocated across these institutions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Canadian dollar is fully convertible. Canada has maintained no exchange controls since repeal of the Foreign Exchange Control Act in 1951 and is an IMF Article VIII member. No licensing or prior approval distinguishes current-account versus capital-account transactions; profit repatriation via ULC dividends is free from exchange-control hurdles. The only fiscal frictions are Part XIII non-resident dividend withholding tax (25% statutory, treaty-reducible, with ULC dividend-recharacterization risk under hybrid-entity rules) and bank-level FINTRAC electronic funds transfer (EFT) reporting for cross-border wires of C$10,000 or more.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No surrender or mandatory-conversion regime exists in Canada. Export and consulting-fee proceeds may be retained indefinitely in foreign currency, whether onshore or offshore; no statutory timeline or conversion ratio applies. The sole compliance burden is FINTRAC EFT reporting for each cross-border transfer of C$10,000 or more within a 24-hour period, plus Statistics Canada balance-of-payments statistical reporting. These requirements are informational only and do not restrict holding or deployment of export receipts.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Royal Bank of Canada (RBC Royal Bank)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Wise Business (Wise Canada Inc.) is the designated B2B rail and is technically viable but legally constrained: Wise holds no OSFI banking licence and operates as a FINTRAC-registered money services business (MSB), safeguarding client funds at Schedule I banks without CDIC deposit insurance. Feasibility is High for low-value, high-volume cross-border consulting disbursements and fee collection in 40+ currencies via local clearing, but Medium for high-value capital flows because Wise lacks Canadian escrow or trust account capabilities and cannot host a capital escrow account. The ULC must complete Wise business validation, including UBO disclosure, registry extract, and linkage to a verified Schedule I operating account.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: No absolute statutory in-person requirement exists under the PCMLTFA; banks apply a risk-based approach. However, because the ULC is an uncommon unlimited-liability structure with non-resident ownership, Schedule I banks generally impose enhanced due diligence requiring (i) a video or in-branch compliance interview with at least one director, (ii) certified true copies of identification and corporate documents attested by a Canadian notary public or bank branch, and (iii) live Alberta Corporate Registry verification. Fully remote onboarding is possible at RBC, TD, and ATB for Low-Risk Standard entities, but for ULCs it remains discretionary and usually conditioned on a cleared video KYC interview.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unlimited-liability hybrid corporate structure (ULC) with pass-through tax election interpreted as tax-avoidance or hybrid-mismatch red flag.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide Alberta Certificate of Incorporation and Articles filed under the Business Corporations Act (Alberta), a current Corporate Registry search abstract confirming good standing, the executed ULC tax-election statement, a cross-border tax memorandum addressing hybrid-entity dividend recharacterization risk, a written economic-substance narrative (Alberta office, payroll, client contracts), and prior-year corporate filings or nil-return confirmation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Layered non-resident ultimate beneficial ownership (UBO) obscuring the natural-person controller.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deliver a FINTRAC-aligned UBO register (full legal name, date of birth, nationality, residential address, passport copy, and complete control chain), certified corporate registry extracts for every intermediate foreign holding entity, certified English translations where applicable, and a signed directors attestation of control and source of wealth.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Zero or minimal paid-up capital combined with high-value inbound capital injections disproportionate to declared consultancy revenue.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: File a capital-introduction memorandum, source-of-wealth statements (personal bank statements and tax returns) for each funding shareholder, the executed share subscription agreement, escrow release instructions, a 12-month cash-flow projection linked to signed market-entry consulting contracts, and evidence of underlying client engagements.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border consulting receipts from, or trade payments to, higher-risk foreign jurisdictions that may suggest sanctions evasion or trade-based money laundering.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide jurisdiction risk scorecards for each target market, full client KYC files (signed contracts, invoices, sanctions and PEP screening output), a documented transaction-monitoring framework, monthly narrative reports describing the commercial purpose of each payment flow, and a register of all wire reference codes to support bank-filed FINTRAC EFT reports.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Foreign shareholders remit via SWIFT MT103 to the ULC operational account at a Schedule I bank (RBC, TD, or ATB) using the wire instruction 'Issued Capital Contribution - ULC', including the Alberta institution number, transit number, and account number. No exchange-control approval is required. Funds intended for staged deployment should first clear through a dedicated Capital Escrow Account at ATB Financial, released only upon Alberta Corporate Registry verification and a board resolution. Each inbound wire of C$10,000 or more is reported by the bank to FINTRAC as an EFT; the bank classifies the transfer under Statistics Canada balance-of-payments purpose codes.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Client settlement and trade payments flow through two rails: (i) commercial bank wires via SWIFT MT103 from the Schedule I operating account for high-value and institutional payments, and (ii) Wise B2B local-currency rails for sub-C$50,000 disbursements in 40+ currencies. CAD high-value clearing uses the Lynx RTGS system operated by Payments Canada; retail and lower-value CAD settlement uses Payments Canada EFT rails. Commercial letters of credit under UCP600 are atypical for ISIC 7020 consulting services and are used only where institutional clients require bank-issued guarantees. Every outbound wire of C$10,000 or more triggers bank-filed FINTRAC EFT reporting.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable CAD/USD, CAD/GBP, and CAD/EUR currency forwards (up to 24 months) executed under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement with a Schedule I bank
Plain-vanilla European-style FX call and put options on CAD crosses
Cross-currency swaps and cross-currency interest-rate swaps matching long-term USD or EUR consulting receivables
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for non-convertible or restricted emerging-market currency legs paired with CAD or USD; CAD itself is not an NDF-eligible currency because of full convertibility

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of Companies, Alberta Corporate Registry (Service Alberta)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the anniversary of incorporation or amalgamation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: CAD 100 late fee if filed after the 60-day window; failure to file for two consecutive years may result in administrative dissolution by the Registrar.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return (federal and Alberta provincial corporate income tax)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the corporation's fiscal year-end; tax balance is generally due two months after year-end, or three months for a Canadian-controlled private corporation eligible for the small business deduction.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per month for up to 12 months; repeat offenders face an increased 10% penalty plus 2% per month. Daily compound interest applies to unpaid balances.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No revenue-based audit threshold applies. A private Alberta ULC must appoint an auditor unless all shareholders waive the audit requirement. Audited financial statements are mandatory for public companies and when shareholders holding at least 5% of the shares so request.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS or ASPE (Part II of the CPA Canada Handbook) at the corporation's election; private ULCs commonly apply ASPE, while IFRS is required for publicly accountable enterprises.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Alberta's Business Corporations Act requires the ULC to maintain and update a Register of Individuals with Significant Control (ISC) within 15 days of any change. The Alberta Annual Return verifies the registered office and directors and confirms the ISC register is current. Share transfers require updating the Register of Members and the ISC register; no separate annual UBO filing is made to the Alberta Corporate Registry.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Individuals with Significant Control (ISC)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,750 - 9,000 (full audit); USD 0 if shareholder audit waiver is in place

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 0% at the ULC entity level due to pass-through treatment for Alberta Unlimited Liability Corporations
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Shareholders eligible for federal small business deduction (active business income up to CAD 500,000) and Alberta provincial tax incentives

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return filed electronically through CRA My Business Account portal
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: 6 months after the end of the fiscal year

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Aggregate revenue from all sources including consulting fees and market entry activities
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Income allocated to non-resident shareholders reported on personal Canadian tax returns; no corporate tax liability at ULC level
Expenses deductible at shareholder level; no entity-level deductions for pass-through entities

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: CAD 60 per day late filing penalty (maximum CAD 3,000), plus 5% per month interest on unpaid taxes

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: Not applicable; distributions from ULC treated as partnership income with no withholding tax
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: N/A; income flows through to shareholders who report directly. No dividend withholding tax certificate required
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory rate 25% for royalties and interest paid to non-residents; treaty relief available (0-15% under most DTAs). Submit TRC application to CRA

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: CAD 500,000 for related-party transactions requiring local file documentation
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: No dedicated Economic Substance Regulations; compliance enforced via GAAR, transfer pricing adjustments, and CFC rules

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Willful failure to report income or understating taxable income
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fines up to CAD 5 million or imprisonment up to 2 years for individuals; corporate penalties up to CAD 25 million
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors personally liable for willful misrepresentation; potential criminal charges, restitution orders, and director disqualifications

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Personal liability for tax underpayments, possible imprisonment for fraudulent schemes, and travel restrictions under certain acts

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to conduct proper customer due diligence or suspicious transaction reporting

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors can face personal criminal liability, fines, and disqualification from corporate roles

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to maintain TP documentation or apply arm's length principle to related party transactions
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Penalties of 10-50% of the tax shortfall; interest on underpayments
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors personally liable for authorizing non-compliant positions; potential civil and criminal penalties
